drafted_from: tool:fulfill-setup-access's row in tools/app-release-access/tool-rows.json (verify: needs-a-machine), read-data/setup-access.mjs and test/setup-access.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Arrange TestFlight beta access for setup request request-one of account account-one on release source native-ios, app ai.fixture.ios, group Founding members." It runs tool:fulfill-setup-access, which never takes an email address; today it refuses before any Apple call until the engine serves the release owner's claim, checkpoint and finish operations.
no_lists_because: It keeps and reads no list of yours: the person's request, consent and verified email live in the release owner's server-side claim, not in a list the tool is given.
instructions: 1. Get the setup-access request id from the person's setup (request_id), their account_id and the release source (native-ios), plus the app's bundle_identifier and the TestFlight group names the release owner keeps. Give no email: an input that names any other field is refused.
2. Say to your AI: "Arrange beta access for request request-one." The AI calls tools:run at @workshop-tools with tool tool:fulfill-setup-access and those five inputs.

3. Read the answer: state is one of available, invited, accepted, installed, awaiting-invitation, blocked, indeterminate or revoked, with a reason in plain words and the request_id; it never holds the email. On indeterminate, run it again: it reads the tester's state back and never sends a second invitation.

4. Until the engine's records door serves the setup-access operations, every run stops with the error "not operations a tool run can reach at the records door yet. No provider action was taken."; take no step by hand at Apple.

worked_examples.title: A run today is refused before any Apple call
worked_examples.ask: Arrange beta access for request request-one.
worked_examples.given: From tools/app-release-access/test/setup-access.test.mjs (with no setup-access operation at the records door, the tool refuses before any provider call): the tool's default operator is used, so the claim step throws. The same file's native host test shows the path once the operator exists: claim, checkpoint (enroll), finish, ending in state invited.
worked_examples.hands_back: An error, no state: "The release owner's setup-access claim, checkpoint and finish are not operations a tool run can reach at the records door yet. No provider action was taken."
